summary.headline: Tata Elxsi Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR 1,055.7 crore, up 2.3% in constant currency; EBITDA margin 21.9%, up 70 bps QoQ.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 1,055.7 crore, growing 2.3% in constant currency, with all three verticals up sequentially (transportation +2% QoQ, media and communication +3.4%, healthcare and life sciences +3.5%). EBITDA was INR 231.4 crore, up 7.1% QoQ and 19.7% YoY, with margin at 21.9%. Management attributed about 60-70 bps of the margin gain to currency and 10-20 bps to operating leverage and fading one-offs, which absorbed an annual wage revision. Europe automotive remained soft and the transportation outlook depends on it; management expects H2 to exceed H1 across businesses except the Europe-dependent part of transportation.

financial_highlights.change: +2.3% constant currency (QoQ growth per management's framing)
Up from previous quarter; peak pre-COVID ~81-82%

segments.name: Transportation
segments.commentary: Grew 2% QoQ in constant currency, driven by auto OEMs in US and India; Japan flattish, rest of Asia flat, Europe soft. Aerospace and defence adjacency is growing from a small base and is not yet quantified.

segments.name: Media and Communication
segments.commentary: Grew 3.4% QoQ in constant currency on ramp-ups of closed deals and AI-led wins, including a GenAI virtual assistant engagement with a global technology leader.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 3.5% QoQ in constant currency after bottoming last quarter; win with a global renal care leader for next-gen home dialysis systems.

guidance_outlook: Company does not provide guidance as a policy; no guidance revision.
Management expects H2 FY27 revenue to exceed H1 (and therefore be higher YoY in H2), with growth in US, India and Asia; transportation H2 depends on Europe.
Margins expected to improve gradually via operational leverage, utilisation gains and pyramid correction over the next 2-3 quarters; no margin number given.
Wage revision is complete for the year; no material employee cost movement expected in rest of FY27 beyond selective investment.
Q3 is a short quarter with fewer working days; customer-specific furlough decisions awaited.
capex_capacity: Utilisation about 78%, up QoQ; management sees headroom versus pre-COVID peak of about 81-82%.
Pyramid rebalancing planned over next half-year, moving engagements to junior staff and using a bench trained at lower levels.
Deal ramp-ups typically take 2-3 quarters to reach full run-rate; aerospace programmes need at least 2-3 quarters to ramp.
Onsite-offshore revenue mix steady at roughly 25:75.
demand_pricing: Automotive: new multi-year deal from a leading automotive OEM for a cloud-based telematics and connected vehicle ecosystem, not yet ramped up.
Europe: large automotive deals in the final shortlist but unsigned; decision-making delayed by OEM situation; no ramp-downs on signed Europe deals, but some project run-offs.
Aerospace: collaboration with Sarla Aviation on Shunya eVTOL; global aerospace supplier engagement for test rig and validation; growth not disclosed due to small base.
AI demand: enterprises still earmarking AI budgets that partly compete with ER&D discretionary spend, but buying is becoming more ROI-focused.
Leakage: improved YoY, as multi-year large deals protect the base and supplier-side automotive revenue losses have largely shifted to OEMs.
Talent: strong demand for ER&D talent from GCCs; retention focus. Senior-level pay largely variable.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is growth and what drove margin expansion despite wage hikes; how much one-off reversal is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70 bps of margin gain came from currency, 10-20 bps from operational leverage and one-offs fading; wage hikes were offset. Operational leverage expected to continue, with a slightly upward margin trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Did the quarter pan out as planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Media and communication and healthcare were in line with confidence from closed deals; automotive was the uncertain piece, but US and India deal wins helped deliver growth.

qa_highlights.question: Are signed deals sufficient for growth or are new wins needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are needed: ramp-ups take 2-3 quarters and project run-offs require replacement wins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the steady-state margin improve with new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: New deals are innovation and product engineering, with margins described as reasonably flat; margin gains would come from pyramid rebalancing and utilisation across the organisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there guidance revision for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; company does not provide guidance as a policy.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration and health of group customers (Tata Motors, JLR)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JLR is facing its own challenges and is being watched; much of automotive growth comes from outside group customers. Revenue concentration not disclosed.

risks_watch: Europe automotive: large deals unsigned and decision delays persist; timing uncertain.
JLR business performance and layoffs; impact on group-customer spend visible across H2.
Q3 furloughs and short working days could pressure revenue.
Healthcare concentration: only just stabilised, with diversification still early.
Wage cost structure: employee cost per head rising ahead of revenue; margin recovery relies on utilisation and pyramid correction.
Aerospace and BESS/manufacturing growth not disclosed; small base makes it hard to track.
summary.management_tone: Confident on US, India and non-automotive verticals and on H2 being better than H1, but cautious and noncommittal on Europe automotive timing and on margin numbers, which were withheld.
key_quotes: And I think that is the confidence that we carry beyond anything else.
So this is a work in progress, but yes, we will have to progressively move towards, over the next, I would say, 2 to 3 quarters, we will see that gradual improvement in our margins, right?
As a policy, and in general, we don't provide guidance at all.

growth.why: Management qualitatively guides H2 FY27 revenue above H1 (implying higher YoY in H2) with no numeric guidance, backed partly by ramping signed deals and a new automotive telematics deal, while Europe automotive decisions remain delayed and no capacity additions were announced.
